turns.message:
You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

# Continual Harness State

Local continual harness entries belong to this Prime Agent session. Global continual harness entries persist across Prime Agent sessions.
The continual harness entries below are compact summaries, not full descriptions. Use them as routing/context hints; inspect or refine the underlying continual harness entry only when detail matters.
Default to local continual harness refinement for current task progress, temporary blockers, and session coordination. Use global continual harness refinement only for stable cross-session lessons, durable user preferences, reusable skills/subagents, or explicitly project-qualified facts.
Use these continual harness prompt notes, memories, skills, and subagent specs when they are relevant. The base system prompt is immutable; prompt entries below are supplemental notes only.

When to call `await refine.run()`: after a repeated failure, a reusable tactic emerges, a repeated delegation role should become a subagent spec, a repeated procedure should become a skill, a durable fact/preference should become a memory, a narrow behavioral policy should become a prompt addendum, a user corrects behavior that should persist locally or globally, validation shows a continual harness entry is wrong, or a skill/subagent/memory/prompt note should be created, updated, deleted, or rolled back. Keep `await refine.run()` continual harness edits small and evidence-backed.

Call contract: read each installed Python skill's SKILL.md and call its documented module function in the Python REPL; do not assume a `.run` entrypoint. Use `<skill_import> ...` in shell when a CLI exists. Continual harness skill entries are Python REPL skills with an explicit Python `reference` and `arguments` contract. Spawn a continual harness subagent spec by composing a concise task prompt and calling `handle = await rlm.spawn('sub-task', name='worker')`; admission returns immediately with `rlm_child_id`, `name`, `session_dir`, and `model`, never the child's answer. Results arrive only through explicit `agent_message` replies or files; children reply with `await agent_message.send(message, receiver_role='parent')`. Use `await rlm.list_subagents()` to recover direct child handles and `await agent_message.send(..., receiver_role='child', receiver_name=handle.name)` for follow-ups. Do not invent wrappers such as `call_skill(...)`, `run_subagent(...)`, or named subagent registries.

[HarnessEntry(id='arc_task_8a59eaa1_replicate_marked_tile_throughout_separator_grid', kind='memory', title='ARC task-8a59eaa1: replicate marked tile throughout separator grid', content="For ARC task-8a59eaa1, a grid is divided by full straight separator lines into equal-sized rectangular tiles. One tile contains a pattern and the other tiles are blank (background-filled). Copy the pattern tile exactly into every tile, preserving separator lines and leaving dimensions unchanged. The source tile need not be the top-left one: in the test it was the upper-middle tile. Demo: an 8x26 grid split into three 8x8 panels by color-4 columns; pattern in left panel was repeated exactly in middle and right. Test: 9x11 split into 3 columns x 2 rows of 4x3 tiles by color-1 row/columns; upper-middle tile held the pattern and was copied to the other five tiles. My first wrong answer mistakenly read the marked pattern as belonging to upper-left tile, shifting its first row; carefully inspect which tile actually contains the anomaly/pattern before copying.

Additional accepted test (9x11): the grid was split by color-1 separator row 4 and columns 3,7 into six 4x3 panels on background 6. The upper-middle panel was the source, with local pattern rows [9,6,6], [6,6,9], [3,6,6], [6,7,6]. Repeat those exact four rows into all six panels, preserving separators; accepted on the second submission. Important: locate the actual populated panel and copy its exact local pattern; here the first row's 9 is at local column 0, not column 1.", path='general', scope='global', reference={}, arguments={}, metadata={}, source='agent', created_at='2026-10-20T14:24:14.321394+00:00', updated_at='2026-10-20T14:24:26.427834+00:00', version=2), HarnessEntry(id='arc_task_8a59eaa1_repeat_motif_across_divider_separated_panels', kind='memory', title='ARC task-8a59eaa1: repeat motif across divider-separated panels', content="For ARC task-8a59eaa1, color-3 full rows/columns divide a grid into equal panels (in the demo, a full color-3 row and column made four equal quadrants). Additional accepted test: a 23x5 grid used color 2 full dividers at column 2 and rows 7 and 15, making six 7x2 panels on color-1 background. The middle-right panel contained the motif at panel-local coordinates (0,1)=3, (1,0)=6, (1,1)=6, (3,0)=9, and (5,1)=8. Make all six panels identical by copying this exact motif to the corresponding local positions in the other five panels; leave all color-2 divider cells and other background cells unchanged. The initial mistaken guess marked only top-zero/bottom-6 coordinates; correction is nonzero/nonzero.', path='general', scope='global', reference={}, arguments={}, metadata={}, source='agent', created_at='2026-10-20T14:12:03.905387+00:00', updated_at='2026-10-20T14:26:10.604646+00:00', version=2), HarnessEntry(id='arc_task_c3e8f639_decode_3x3_cells_by_ignoring_color_5', kind='memory', title='ARC task-c3e8f639: decode 3x3 cells by ignoring color 5', content='For ARC task-c3e8f639, the input is a grid tiled into 3x3 cells. Produce an output grid with one cell per 3x3 input block. In each block, ignore color 5, which is the background, and output the single remaining color present (including 0 as a valid output color). The demo was 24x24 -> 8x8 and the test was 21x21 -> 7x7; every macro-cell contained only one non-5 color, so this is a direct 3x3-to-1x1 compression. Example test output was [[0,3,0,0,0,0,0],[0,0,3,2,0,0,0],[2,0,0,9,0,0,2],[9,3,0,2,0,0,0],[0,2,9,0,0,9,0],[2,3,2,0,0,9,0],[0,0,0,0,2,0,9]].

Additional accepted test (6x6 -> 2x2): split from top-left into four aligned 3x3 tiles; ignore 5 and emit the sole other color, with 0 retained as a valid result. Test input tiles decoded to [[0,1],[0,0]]; the 1 occurred once in the upper-right tile, and all other tiles contained only 0 and 5. Correct on first submission with no demos. This confirms very small 6x6 cases use the same exact 3x3 compression.', path='general', scope='global', reference={}, arguments={}, metadata={}, source='agent', created_at='2026-10-20T14:23:07.809942+00:00', updated_at='2026-10-20T14:24:41.077506+00:00', version=2), HarnessEntry(id='arc_task_df66f7e9_overlap_bitmap_panels_across_uniform_divider', kind='memory', title='ARC task-df66f7e9: overlap bitmap panels across uniform divider', content='For ARC task-df66f7e9, input contains two equal-sized binary-pattern panels separated by a uniform full row or column of a distinct color. Output is their cellwise intersection: put color 2 where both corresponding panel cells are nonzero; put 0 otherwise. Drop the divider and output panel-sized dimensions. Divider orientation varies: e.g. the 9x2 test has row 4 [7,7] as a horizontal divider, panels rows 0-3 and 5-8; their overlap is [[0,0],[0,0],[0,0],[0,2]]. Demos also show vertical dividers (e.g. col 9, 5, or 4) with left/right panels; output marks only aligned occupied cells in both panels as 2. Output rows concatenate UL/UR for the first n rows, then LL/LR for the next n.', path='general', scope='global', reference={}, arguments={}, metadata={}, source='agent', created_at='2026-10-20T14:07:23.081427+00:00', updated_at='2026-10-20T14:07:23.081441+00:00', version=1), HarnessEntry(id='arc_task_276f8e5f_extend_markers_toward_edge_bars', kind='memory', title='ARC task-276f8e5f: extend markers toward edge bars', content="For task-276f8e5f, a uniform field has two same-colored perpendicular edge bars in opposite corner regions and sparse cells of another color in the region by one bar. Extend each sparse marker horizontally through the background toward its adjacent edge bar, using the marker color for intervening cells; recolor the original marker to 4. Also copy the row-occupancy pattern of those markers, aligned by row offset within their edge-bar segment, into the opposite edge-bar segment: draw marker-color horizontal rays across that segment from its bar to the far edge on each corresponding row. Preserve the bar cells and all unrelated cells. Demonstration: 15x9 field 5, bars of 8 at right rows0-4 and left rows10-14, sparse 1s at (10,5),(12,3),(13,6),(14,4). Rays from each 1 leftward to the 8 bar recolor each 1 to 4; matching row offsets 0,2,3,4 are filled with 1 across rows0,2,3,4 to the right-side bar, leaving row1 unchanged. Another demo uses left-top/right-bottom bars of 5, sparse 2 markers near right-bottom bar, and does the same with color2. In test task input, rows0-3 col0 are 5, rows6-9 col5 are 5, dots of 2 at (6,1),(7,2),(8,1),(9,1): fill rows0-3 cols1-5 with 2; fill lower rows toward right 5 bar with 2 and turn dots to 4.

Accepted test instance (task-276f8e5f): 11x7 field of 5, zero edge bars at right rows 0–2 (column 6) and left rows 4–6 (column 0), sparse 7 markers at (4,3) and (5,3). Fill rows 0 and 1 across columns 0–5 with 7, preserving the right-edge zeros. Extend each marker leftward: set columns 1–2 to 7 and recolor each original marker at column 3 to 4; preserve left-edge zeros and all other cells. Rows 2 onward otherwise remain unchanged. This output was accepted. The row offsets occupied by the markers in the left bar segment are copied across the opposite segment from its edge bar; original markers become 4.

Accepted 20x19 instance (background 5, bars 6, markers 9): top boundary bar at row 0, cols 9–17; opposite bottom bar at row 19, cols 0–8; markers at (4,14),(7,17),(9,16),(14,13),(17,12). Treat this as the rotated orientation of the edge-bar projection rule: each marker is in the segment aligned with the top bar, so draw a 9 ray vertically upward from row 1 to just before its marker, recolor the marker to 4, and leave cells beyond it unchanged. Copy marker column offsets relative to the top bar's left endpoint (cols 12–17 offsets 3,4,5,7,8) to the opposite bottom bar segment (cols 3,4,5,7,8); draw 9 upward from row 18 through row 0 in those columns, preserving both 6 bars. This output was accepted. Bar segment alignment uses left-to-right offset, even though the bars occupy opposite halves.

Accepted 24x27 instance (background 3, edge bars 9, marker color 7): right bar at col 26 rows 2–11 and left bar at col 0 rows 14–23; markers at (2,11),(3,23),(4,17),(6,23),(8,3),(11,15). Each marker lies in the right-bar segment: draw 7 rightward through the cells before col 26, and change the original marker to 4. Their row offsets 0,1,2,4,6,9 map to rows 14,15,16,18,20,23 of the opposite left-bar segment; fill columns 1–26 with 7 on those rows, preserving col 0 bar. This exact test output was accepted.

Accepted 24x27 instance (background 3, edge bars 9, marker color 7): right bar at col 26 rows 2–11 and left bar at col 0 rows 14–23; markers at (2,11),(3,23),(4,17),(6,23),(8,3),(11,15). Each marker lies in the right-bar segment: draw 7 rightward through the cells before col 26, and change the original marker to 4.
